items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: You know jazz was very important in helping to break down some social barriers, racial barriers, even preceded Jackie Robinson.

ctx.x: Right. There’s a lot of that. Joe Wilder doesn’t take on that. He doesn’t take on that attitude. Buster Cooper, he didn’t take on that attitude. Britt Woodman, he didn’t take on that attitude. But some of the guys that are under him, it seems like they’re bitter, it’s like hey man, you could not be playing jazz at all. I mean things haven’t always been great. I mean just like in life, there’s ups and there’s downs, but you take the good with the bad and you just try to roll with it. And I think that’s the spirit…

You know jazz was very important in helping to break down some social barriers, racial barriers, even preceded Jackie Robinson. Where is the state of that in music now for you? From what you see anyway?

I think, I guess there’s elements of everything that existed before that are still — but me personally I haven’t really experienced much of anything that’s negative. I haven’t always been happy with anything from my playing to well maybe well I didn’t get this gig or it didn’t work out or a promoter didn’t pay me. You know, things happen. But I think it all depends on how you look at life. Do you want to be a person that’s going to live and complain about your condition or whatever the conditions are or do you…
